### Observed differences

- A08 disappeared from the observed behaviour: earlier it ran in about 71 in 100 traces (about 1.1 executions per trace, almost always at the very start of the case — median position 1); in the later window it is not observed in any of the 200 traces. [OCC001, POS001]
- A07's routing changed completely: earlier, all 219 observed outgoing transitions of A07 went to A08; in the later window none of its 97 observed transitions do, going instead to A05 (about 39 in 100), A03 (about 27), A04 (about 22) and A02 (about 12). [DIR001, DIR002]
- A08's relations collapsed: earlier it co-occurred with A07 in about 70 in 100 traces and with A05, A04 or A03 in about 29–33 in 100; in the later window it co-occurs with none of them, A07 appears without it in about 67 in 100 traces, and A05, A04 and A03 each appear alone in about 32–33 in 100 — down from roughly six in ten traces earlier for each of them. [REL004, REL003, REL002, REL001]
- Downstream work moved closer to A07: A05 now follows A07 one step later in about 42 in 100 observed pairs (earlier typically 2–3 steps), A03 one step later in about 43 in 100 (earlier mostly 2), and A04 at 1–2 steps (earlier 2–3). [LAG004, LAG002, LAG003]
- Repetitions also tightened: A07-to-A07 repetitions moved from 4–5 steps apart to 3–4, and A04-to-A04 from 3–5 to 2–4, though the latter rests on only about 17–18 observed pairs per window. [LAG005, LAG001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that A08 is no longer executed in the later window: it previously ran in about seven in ten cases and is now absent from all 200 later traces, and the flow that ran through it — A07 always handing over to A08, with A05, A04 and A03 further downstream — now runs directly from A07 to A05, A04, A03 and A02, with those activities following A07 about one step sooner than they followed the old A07→A08 sequence. The signs are direct (occurrence, position and outgoing-transition items all show the disappearance), consistent (all four relation items show co-occurrence with A08 dropping to zero), and the 13 qualifying items far exceed the roughly 0.21 expected by chance in an unchanged process, so the pattern as a whole is not what random sampling produces. [OCC001, POS001, DIR001, DIR002, REL004, REL003, REL002, REL001, LAG004, LAG002, LAG003]

Limitations: zero participation establishes only that A08 was not observed in the later window, so a genuine removal cannot be separated from A08 becoming very rare or all later cases following a variant without it; most items describe the same underlying trace behaviour rather than independent confirmations; and the A04 repetition item rests on few observations. [OCC001, LAG001]

Setup:

- Screening: 42 units tested, 13 items qualified, 0.21 expected by chance. That's a count many times larger than the expectation (13 vs 0.21, ~60x). So the screening comparison says the number of items cannot be explained by chance. So we move past "insufficient evidence" based on count.

All items are control-flow family. No time or resource items (no TWAIT, ASSIGN, CONC, HAND). So I should not discuss time or resources.

Now let's understand the evidence:

OCC001: A08 occurrences. Before: mean occurrences per trace 1.095, trace participation 0.705 (about 71 in 100 traces), recurrence support 0.245. After: all zero. Support before 141, after 0. So A08 disappeared entirely from the later window — not observed at all.

POS001: A08 position. Before support 0.705, median position 1.0 (i.e., A08 typically at position ~1, early in the trace). After: support 0. A08 gone.

DIR002: A08 outgoing transitions. Before: A08 → A05 (0.358), A08 → A03 (0.349), A08 → A04 (0.193), A08 → A02 (0.101). After: empty profile. A08 gone, so no outgoing transitions.

DIR001: A07 outgoing transitions. Before: A07 → A08 with share 1.0 (all observed outgoing transitions of A07 went to A08). After: A07 → A05 (0.392), A07 → A04 (0.216), A07 → A02 (0.124), A07 → A03 (0.268). A08 no longer a successor. Support before 219 outgoing transitions, after 97.

REL004: A07 & A08 relation. Before: cooccurrence 0.705, A_before_B (A07 before A08) 0.46, interleaved 0.245, neither 0.295. After: cooccurrence 0.0, A_only (A07 only) 0.67, neither 0.33. So A07 now occurs without A08 in about 67 in 100 traces.

REL003: A05 & A08. Before: cooccurrence 0.325, B_only (A08 only) 0.38, A_only 0.035, interleaved 0.205, neither 0.26. After: A_only (A05 only) 0.33, neither 0.67. So A05 now occurs without A08.

REL002: A04 & A08. Before: cooccurrence 0.325, B_only 0.38, A_only 0.05, interleaved 0.19, neither 0.245. After: A_only 0.315, neither 0.685.

REL001: A03 & A08. Before: cooccurrence 0.29, B_only 0.415, A_only 0.045, interleaved 0.215, neither 0.25. After: A_only 0.33, neither 0.67.

So the pattern: A08 was present in ~70% of traces before (often early, median position 1), and A07 always followed A08 (A07's only observed successor was A08). After, A08 is completely absent, and A07 now leads to A05, A04, A02, A03.

LAG items:
LAG003: A07 → A04 lag. Before: mostly lag 2 (0.367) and 3 (0.469). After: lag 1 (0.211), 2 (0.329), 4 (0.005), 5 (0.070). Hmm, wait — before, A07→A04 within five steps: lags 2-3. After: lags 1, 2, 4, 5. Support before 41, after 40.

Wait, but before, A07's only successor was A08. So how did A07→A04 occur within 5 steps before? LAG is ordered pair within five steps, not necessarily direct successor. So A07 ... A04 within 5 steps. Before, A07 was followed by A08 (directly), and A04 might come a bit later. After, A07 directly precedes A04 sometimes (lag 1: 0.211).

LAG004: A07 → A05. Before: lag 2 (0.6), 3 (0.236), 4 (0.018). After: lag 1 (0.416), 2 (0.127), 3 (0.02), 4 (0.025), 5 (0.053). So A05 moved closer to A07 — now often immediately after (lag 1 in ~42% of observed pairs).

LAG002: A07 → A03. Before: lag 2 (0.593), 3 (0.162), 4 (0.079). After: lag 1 (0.433), 2 (0.193), 3 (0.041), 4 (0.027), 5 (0.041). Same pattern: A03 now often immediately after A07.

LAG005: A07 → A07 (repetition). Before: lag 4 (0.317), 5 (0.356). After: lag 3 (0.406), 4 (0.323). So repetitions of A07 got closer together. Support before 39, after 35.

LAG001: A04 → A04 (repetition). Before: lag 3 (0.101), 4 (0.362), 5 (0.275). After: lag 2 (0.117), 3 (0.333), 4 (0.179), 5 (0.037). Repetitions closer. Support before 17, after 18 — small support, weak.

So the main hypothesis: A08 was removed from the process (or became unobserved) in the later window. Before, A08 occurred in about 70 in 100 traces, typically very early (median position 1), and A07's executions were always followed by A08. In the later window, A08 is not observed at all, A07 now flows directly to A05, A04, A03, A02, and the activities that previously followed A08 (A05, A04, A03) now follow A07 more closely (often at lag 1).

This is a removal/disappearance of an activity, not a shift in path frequencies. The condition for "existing paths taken with different frequencies" doesn't apply because A08 is absent in the after window.

The hypothesis: A08 was removed (became skipped/no longer executed). This is directly supported by OCC001 (participation 0.705 → 0), POS001, DIR002, REL items (cooccurrence → 0, A_only up), and DIR001 (A07's successor changed from exclusively A08 to A05/A04/A03/A02).

Competing explanation: A08 might still exist in the process but was not sampled in the later window (zero participation only means not observed). But with 200 traces and 70% participation before, complete disappearance in 200 traces is very unlikely by chance — though strictly, "zero participation only means the activity was not observed in that window." Also the empirical strength 0.995 for all items — high but that alone doesn't separate real change from rare variant; the screening count does the heavy lifting (13 items vs 0.21 expected).

Support level: The evidence directly and consistently shows A08 disappearing and A07's outgoing behaviour changing.
